subject: Escalation: Nova Oil & Gas — eligibility & deal exceptions request
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0500
Subject: Intro: NovaOG - Private deployment + pricing ask

Team — quick handoff. I met with Pablo Mendes (Procurement) at Nova Oil & Gas LLC yesterday. High level: they want an on-prem / private deployment for data residency and are asking for a sizeable commercial concession. Key points: 

- Requested commercial: 30% discount off list, 2-year committed Dedicated capacity, and an explicit clause removing our standard export control indemnity.
- They are incorporated in a jurisdiction that routes ownership through a Panama entity; their public filings list a beneficial owner with ties to entities in jurisdictions flagged during our initial screening.
- They completed our KYC questionnaire (attached) but flagged some third-party sub-contractors operating in regions we typically screen for export controls.
- Timeline: they want pricing and a draft SOW by 03/24 to meet their board procurement window.

Attachments: novaog_qual_deck.pdf, kyc_questionnaire_filled.pdf

I think this needs legal + security + deal desk oversight — asking Stephanie to escalate. Happy to provide the meeting notes / intro if helpful.

Thanks,
Sergio
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Intro: NovaOG - Private deployment + pricing ask

Thanks for the context, Sergio. A couple of technical/legal flags from infra/security perspective: 

- Private/on-prem is feasible but we need an explicit list of where the on-prem will be hosted and who will have admin/network access. Certain hardware/crypto stacks trigger export control reviews (e.g., HSM + government export restrictions).
- We cannot ship models/weights to locations on sanctioned lists. If any of their operational footprint falls into those jurisdictions, we must block the shipment of restricted model binaries; we can instead offer a hosted (Redwood Dedicated) alternative restricted to approved regions.
- From an engineering delivery standpoint, a 2-week lead for a draft SOW is tight but doable if legal signs off on access controls.

Attaching: infra_requirements.pdf (initial checklist). My recommendation: pause commercial concessions until Compliance confirms there's no sanctions hit on beneficial owners or contractors.

— Dev
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 13:40:00 -0500
Subject: Deal desk packet: NovaOG — requested exceptions and discount

Folks — attaching the deal desk packet and the redlined contract we received from the customer. Summary of commercial asks coming from Procurement: 

1) 30% one-time discount on committed capacity (term: 24 months).
2) Removal of standard export control indemnity (they want us to accept broader liability).
3) On-prem deployment permitted with customer-managed admin accounts.

Our preliminary position: we can consider a capped discount up to 15% for an enterprise commit, but the export indemnity removal and on-prem administrative access are non-starters without legal & security sign-off.

I have included suggested redlines in redlines_contract.docx and a completed dealdesk_spreadsheet.xlsx with the financials. We need an exec-level approval for any deviation from exporting clause and for discounts beyond our standard 15% threshold. 

Attachments: dealdesk_spreadsheet.xlsx, redlines_contract.docx, kyc_questionnaire_filled.pdf

Next step: Stephanie — can you escalate to Grace/Legal with a recommendation? The customer will push for a signature by 03/24 so time is tight.

Thanks,
Rachel
Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Escalation: Exec approval requested for NovaOG (possible sanctions exposure)

Hi Grace / Laura — escalating for an executive decision. Summary below — please see attached deal packet. 

What they ask: 30% discount, removal of our export control indemnity, and on-prem deployment with customer-managed admin. 
Why we escalated: preliminary screening shows a beneficial owner and subcontractor footprint that touch jurisdictions flagged in our sanctions/export-control matrix. Dev calls out that we cannot ship certain model weights to restricted jurisdictions.

Proposed recommendation from Sales Ops/Engineering (my note): 
- Conditional approval only. Do NOT proceed to signature until Compliance completes enhanced screening (beneficial ownership + contractor list).
- If they clear Compliance: approve up to 15% discount (not 30%) and require the customer to sign an Export Compliance Addendum that preserves our indemnity and limits model shipment to approved regions.
- On-prem: allow only if we can maintain technical controls (RBAC, no unrestricted admin keys, and an agreed sweep for model weight distribution).

Time pressure: procurement requests a draft SOW and pricing by 03/24. If Compliance needs more time, offer a committed Dedicated deployment in an approved region as short-term alternative.

Attachments: dealdesk_spreadsheet.xlsx, redlines_contract.docx, novaog_qual_deck.pdf, infra_requirements.pdf

Can you confirm guidance asap (timeline: 24–48 hours)? If you prefer, I can set up a 30-min triage call and include Compliance (Anya from KYC vendor is available).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, Enterprise Accounts (Acting)
Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Escalation: Exec approval requested for NovaOG (possible sanctions exposure)

Thanks for the concise packet and the heads-up. Decision and next steps below: 

1) We will NOT approve the 30% discount or the removal of the export indemnity at this time.
2) Do an enhanced KYC/sanctions screen (including beneficial ownership) through our vendor (Anya / KYC Screening). If the customer clears, Leadership will approve a maximum commercial concession of 10% (one-time credit) subject to: 
   - Execution of an Export Compliance Addendum that preserves our indemnity and restricts model shipment to approved regions only;
   - Technical controls confirmed by Dev: no unmanaged admin keys and proof of RBAC and local logging forwarded to our audit endpoint.
3) On-prem deployment: provisional approval only — legal must draft an SOW addendum that restricts model binaries and requires a security attestation. If we cannot guarantee export-control compliance for the requested deployment locations, the fallback is Dedicated (Redwood-hosted) restricted to allowed regions.
4) Rachel / Marissa: prepare a revised offer (10% max concession) and mark the deal as ESCL-REVIEW in HubSpot. Add a clause requiring funds to be held in escrow or deferred until screenings complete if the customer insists on a quick signature.

Please queue Legal (Laura) to draft the Export Compliance Addendum and SOW redlines. Stephanie — please set a 30-minute triage call with Compliance (Anya), Legal (Laura), and Dev to run through the KYC output as soon as it's available.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
